This page shows how to open the numbered bags and how to use the orange brick separator. It has no model-building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
The top of the page is a preview of what bag 1 and the three base plates build: three minifigures and the apartment's first section. No bricks are placed on this page.
The lower part shows Amy, Bernadette and Howard being assembled from hair, head, torso and legs. None of those minifigure parts are in the parts list, so I recorded nothing for them.
The three base plates in the preview are probably the 16 x 16 plate and the two 6 x 16 plates from the parts list. I will record them on the page where they are first placed.
The top inset on this page is a preview of the finished model, so it adds nothing.
Step 1 uses one large dark tan plate and one 1 x 4 tan plate. I read the large plate as the 6 x 16 plate (lego-3027, the only dark tan plate of that size in the parts list).
The 1 x 4 plate sits on the studs along one short end of the 6 x 16 plate, so it rests on b1.
Step 2 adds the 16 x 16 dark tan plate. The red arrows show it being pushed up against the long edge of the 6 x 16 plate (b1) built in step 1.
The two plates only meet edge to edge. No studs overlap, so it rests on nothing and I listed no joins. Later bricks and plates should bridge them.
The side caption (Leonard quote) is only text and adds no pieces.

Step 3 adds two 2 x 4 tan plates and one 1 x 8 tan plate in a row along the back edge of the 16 x 16 plate (b3). Together they cover its full 16-stud back edge: the 2 x 4s take 8 studs and the 1 x 8 takes the other 8.

The first 2 x 4 starts right at the seam between the 6 x 16 plate (b1) and the 16 x 16 plate (b3), next to the 1 x 4 plate (b2). I read it as sitting on b3 only, since it does not appear to overlap b1's studs.
Step 4 adds the second 6 x 16 dark tan plate. The red arrows show it being pushed against the right edge of the 16 x 16 plate (b3).
As with step 2, the plates only meet edge to edge, so it rests on nothing and I listed no joins.

Step 5 adds two 1 x 8 tan plates (lego-3460). One runs along the back edge. It meets the new 6 x 16 plate (b7) at the corner, where it also covers part of the 16 x 16 plate (b3), so I listed both under rests_on.
The second one turns the corner and runs along the right-hand long edge of b7, so it rests on b7 only.
The drawing is small, so I am not certain of the exact overlap between the first plate and b3. This is my best reading.
Step 6 adds ten tan 2 x 4 plates (b10 to b19), laid as one solid tan floor block over the back-right part of the baseplate. It sits mainly on the second 6 x 16 plate (b7).
It also adds one reddish brown 1 x 4 plate (b20). It sits on the 16 x 16 plate (b3), next to the left end of the tan block.
I read the dark red-brown piece as a Plate 1 x 4 in Reddish Brown (lego-3710), the only matching 1 x 4 plate in the parts list.
I could not tell exactly how the tan block overlaps the seam between b3 and b7. I listed b7 only for every 2 x 4 plate. Some of them may also touch b3.
Step 7 adds three tan plates: a 1 x 4, a 1 x 3 and a 1 x 8. The 1 x 8 is shown in the callout and the arrow points at the front part of the tan floor block.

The drawing is small and does not show which 2 x 4 plate each new plate sits on. I assigned the rests_on links to the tan block plates (b10 to b13) as a best guess. They are on top of the block's front area.
The 1 x 3 is read from the second small icon, which is shorter than the 1 x 4.
Step 8 adds two tan 2 x 4 plates and one tan 4 x 4 round corner plate. They extend the tan floor block toward the front and give its front-left corner a rounded edge.
The drawing does not show exactly which plates lie under the new pieces, so I listed b7 (the plate the block is built on) as rests_on for all three. Some may also touch earlier tan plates.
Step 9 adds a tan 1 x 8 brick, a tan 2 x 2 corner brick and a light bluish gray panel.
The 1 x 8 brick starts the back wall on the 1 x 8 plate (b8). The 2 x 2 corner brick sits at the back-right corner on the corner plates (b8 and b9).

The grey piece looks like Panel 1 x 2 x 1 with rounded corners (lego-4865b), the only light bluish gray flat panel of that shape in the parts list. The arrow places it beside the corner brick, on the right-edge plate b9.
The exact studs each piece covers are my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 10 adds three tan bricks (1 x 8, 1 x 3, 1 x 2) that continue the back wall along the left and middle part of the back edge. The drawing is small, so which plate each brick sits on is my best reading.
It also adds a long reddish brown 1 x 10 plate (lego-4477) lying on the floor across the seam between the left 6 x 16 plate (b1) and the 16 x 16 plate (b3).
The two red 1 x 2 pieces are placed on the floor near the wall. The parts list has no red 1 x 2 plate, only two red 1 x 2 tiles (lego-3069b), so I recorded them as those.
The first red piece is on b1 and the second is on b3.
Step 11 adds three reddish brown 1 x 1 bricks and one orange-brown 1 x 1 brick. They are in a row on the tan floor block in front of the back wall, with the orange-brown one next to the corner.
The orange-brown brick is read as Medium Nougat (lego-3005). It matches the plain 1 x 1 brick colour in the parts list.
The drawing does not show which tan plate is under each brick, so I assigned b10 to b13 as a best guess.
Step 12 adds five tan bricks (two 1 x 8, one 1 x 3, two 1 x 2) as a second course on the back wall. I placed three on the left wall section and two on the right section by the corner.

In the drawing the second course looks staggered over the first, so some bricks may also clutch a neighbouring brick below. I could only read one supporting brick per new brick, so the rests_on links are a best guess.

Step 13 adds a reddish brown 1 x 3 plate and a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate laid across the 1 x 1 bricks from step 11 like a bridge or shelf. The callout shows a reddish brown 1 x 1 brick being pushed onto the 1 x 4 plate.
It also adds a medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry brick (lego-98283) on the orange-brown 1 x 1 brick (b39) at the back corner.
The small drawing does not show exactly which 1 x 1 bricks each plate spans. I assigned the 1 x 4 plate to b36 and b37 and the 1 x 3 plate to b38 and b39 as a best guess.

Step 14 adds a third course to the back wall: two tan 1 x 8 bricks, a tan 1 x 3, a tan 1 x 2 and a tan 2 x 2 corner brick. Three of them go on the left wall section and the other three on the right wall section by the corner.
It also adds an orange-brown 1 x 1 brick on top of the masonry brick (b48) in the corner stack. I read it as Medium Nougat 3005, as in step 11.
The wall bricks are stacked on the matching bricks of the course below. The real build may stagger them over neighbouring bricks, so some rests_on links may be incomplete.

Step 15 builds a small stack on the reddish brown shelf plate. From bottom to top it is a dark tan 1 x 2 jumper plate, a medium blue 1 x 2 jumper plate, and a red 1 x 2 tile. The callout shows them being stacked in that order.
It also adds one reddish brown 1 x 1 brick beside the stack. I placed it on the 1 x 3 shelf plate (b45).
The grey-brown piece at the bottom of the callout is read as the Dark Tan jumper plate, the only 1 x 2 jumper plate in a brownish-grey colour in the parts list.
I could not tell exactly which plate sits under the stack, so b46 is a best guess.

Step 16 builds a row of small plates on their sides to look like books on the shelf. The three callouts show: (1) the pin going into the reddish brown Technic brick, (2) a red plate being pushed onto a dark green plate, (3) a dark bluish gray tile going onto the end of the row.

The sideways attachments are not resting-on joins, so they are in other_joins. Only the Technic brick (b59) sits on the shelf plate (b46). I am not sure of the exact order of colours in the row. This chain is my best reading of the small callouts.

The first icon is a red 1 x 1 plate, the second a dark blue 1 x 1 plate, the third a dark bluish gray 1 x 1 tile, the fourth a Technic pin, the fifth a reddish brown Technic brick with a pin hole, and the sixth a dark green 1 x 1 plate.

Step 17 adds three reddish brown 1 x 1 plates as caps on the small reddish brown posts of the bookshelf. The arrow shows one being pressed onto the right-hand post, and the other two go on the other posts.
The picture is small, so which post gets which plate is a best guess. I put them on the 1 x 1 brick from step 13 (b47), the 1 x 1 brick from step 15 (b58) and the Technic brick (b59).

Step 18 adds a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate across the tops of the bookshelf posts to make the top shelf. It also adds one more reddish brown 1 x 1 plate on a post. The arrow points to the right-hand post.
The icon shows a 1 x 4 plate and a 1 x 1 plate. Which posts each one sits on is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 19 adds a fourth course to the back wall: two tan 1 x 8 bricks, a tan 1 x 3, a tan 1 x 2 and two tan 1 x 1 bricks with a stud on one side (lego-87087). The side-stud bricks are the ones shown with a round mark on the face at the left end of the right wall section.
It also adds a medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry brick (lego-98283) on top of the orange-brown corner stack (b54).

Where each brick sits in the wall is my best reading of the small drawing. I stacked the new bricks on the brick directly below. The 1 x 8 on the right wall section also touches the corner brick (b53).

Step 20 repeats the step 16 idea on the upper shelf. A reddish brown 1 x 4 plate goes on top of the shelf and a Technic brick sits on it. A pin goes into the brick, and a row of three small plates is attached sideways: dark green, tan, then blue.
The three callouts show: (1) the pin into the Technic brick, (2) the tan plate onto the dark green plate, and (3) the finished four-piece row.
The blue plate is recorded as a Dark Blue 1 x 1 plate (lego-3024), the only blue 1 x 1 plate in the parts list.
Only the Technic brick (b78) rests on the shelf. The rest of the row is held by the sideways joins listed in other_joins.

Step 21 adds a fifth course to the back wall: one tan 1 x 8, three tan 1 x 3, one tan 1 x 2 and one tan 2 x 2 corner brick. One 1 x 3 sits on the left wall section and the other two sit on the right wall section.
The red arrows show a tan 1 x 2 plate being pressed onto the two side-stud bricks (b74 and b75) at the left end of the right wall section.
It also adds an orange-brown 1 x 1 brick (read as Medium Nougat 3005) on the masonry brick (b76) of the corner stack.
As before, exactly which brick each new piece sits on is my best reading of the small drawing.
Step 22 adds a tan 1 x 2 plate onto the top studs of the wall column on the left of the right wall section. The red arrows point to those studs.
It also adds two reddish brown 1 x 1 bricks and one reddish brown 1 x 1 plate on the bookshelf. They build the shelf posts up one level, with the plate as a cap on one post.

The drawing is small, so the exact supporting pieces are my best reading. In particular, I am not sure whether this tan plate lands on the plate from step 21 or on the 1 x 3 brick beside it. I chose the 1 x 3 brick (b86).

Step 23 adds a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate across the tops of the bookshelf posts to make the top of the shelf. It also adds one reddish brown 1 x 1 plate on the right-hand post, where the arrow points.
The drawing is small, so the exact supporting pieces are my best reading of which posts hold each plate.

Step 24 adds a sixth course to the back wall: two tan 1 x 8 bricks, one tan 1 x 3, three tan 1 x 1 bricks with a stud on one side (lego-87087) and one plain tan 1 x 1 brick. It also adds a medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry brick on top of the corner stack.
One side-stud brick goes at the left end of the left wall section. The other two go at the left end of the right wall section, where the small round side studs show in the picture.
Which brick each new piece sits on is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 25 builds the door. In callout 1 a black round 1 x 1 brick (the knob) goes onto the door handle plinth. In callout 2 a sticker is applied to the door, shown with a flip-over symbol meaning the door is turned over. In callout 3 the door is fitted into the white door frame, and the frame is set into the wall opening.

The door is the nougat (salmon-coloured) Door 1 x 4 x 6 (lego-60616b) and the frame is the white Door Frame 1 x 4 x 6 (lego-60596). The frame stands in the wall opening on the back-edge plates, which I recorded as b4 and b5.
The sticker sheet (lego-23931) is one part in the parts list, so I recorded the applied sticker as a single piece joined to the door.
A tan 1 x 2 plate is pressed onto the studs of the side-stud brick column right of the frame (red arrows). I recorded it as resting on b103.
The supporting pieces under the frame and the plate are my best reading of the small drawing.
Step 26 adds a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate and a reddish brown 1 x 1 brick to the top of the bookshelf, building it up one more level. The page shows no callout, only the finished model.
The exact supporting pieces are my best reading of the small drawing. I put the plate on the previous 1 x 4 plate (b96) and the brick on the previous cap plate (b97).

Step 27 is on the top of the bookshelf. It adds two dark bluish gray 1 x 1 headlight bricks, one reddish brown 1 x 1 brick and one reddish brown Technic brick. All four sit on the top shelf plate (b111).

The Technic brick takes a pin, and three small plates are attached sideways in order: dark green, red, dark blue. The callouts show (1) the pin, (2) the red plate onto the green plate, and (3) the finished row. These are the same 'books' as in steps 16 and 20, and the sideways joins are in other_joins.
The drawing is small, so which of the four pieces sits where on the shelf plate is my best guess.

Step 28 adds a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate over the two dark bluish gray headlight bricks from step 27, and puts the printed 1 x 2 tile with the vintage radio picture (lego-3069bpr0150, Dark Orange) on top of it. It becomes the radio on the shelf.
I read the second icon as the vintage radio print tile because it is the only radio print in the parts list.
The headlight bricks as supports (b113 and b114) are my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 29 adds the white window frame (1 x 4 x 6 with 3 panes) and the clear glass for it. The callout shows the glass being fitted into the frame, and the frame is then set on the tan floor block against the back wall near the corner.
The frame stands on the floor block. I assigned b10 and b11 as the plates it clutches. This is my best guess, since the drawing does not show which plates are underneath.
Step 30 adds a medium nougat 1 x 4 masonry brick, a tan 2 x 2 corner brick and a tan 1 x 1 brick along the right-hand edge of the floor, beside the window. They start a low wall or step on that side.
The pieces sit on the 1 x 8 plate that runs along the right long edge (b9). The exact studs they cover are my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 31 adds a tan 1 x 3 brick, two medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry bricks and one medium nougat 1 x 1 brick. They build up the low wall beside the window from step 30. The page shows no callout, only the finished model.
The icon for the tan brick looks like a 1 x 3 (three studs), so I recorded it as lego-3622.

The two masonry bricks sit on the earlier 1 x 4 masonry brick (b125). The tan 1 x 3 spans the tan corner and 1 x 1 bricks, and the 1 x 1 brick sits on the corner brick. Exact studs are my best reading.

Step 32 adds two reddish brown 1 x 4 bricks, stacked as shown in the callout, and a reddish brown 1 x 2 x 2 panel (lego-87552). They stand on the tan floor block beside the window, and the dark brown pieces look like the start of the sofa.
The panel is the only reddish brown 1 x 2 x 2 panel in the parts list. I identified it from the icon, a 1 x 2 piece with a tall back and side supports.
The drawing does not show which floor plates are under each piece, so b14, b18 and b19 are best guesses from the tan floor block.

Step 33 builds more of the sofa. A reddish brown 2 x 4 plate goes over the stacked 1 x 4 bricks and the panel from step 32. Four reddish brown 1 x 1 headlight bricks are joined in two pairs, and each pair gets a reddish brown 1 x 2 jumper plate on top (callouts 3 and 4).
I read the flat 'dark' icon as the Plate Special 1 x 2 jumper in Reddish Brown (lego-15573), the only reddish brown flat 1 x 2 piece with a single stud.

The callout pictures are small. The side joins between the headlight bricks and where the finished pairs sit on the plate are my best reading. The pairs are recorded as resting on the 2 x 4 plate (b135).
Step 34 adds a tan 1 x 2 brick, a tan 1 x 2 plate with a door rail, a reddish brown 2 x 2 plate and a medium nougat 1 x 4 masonry brick.

The 2 x 2 plate covers the two jumper plates on top of the sofa pieces. The masonry brick goes on the two masonry 1 x 2 bricks of the low wall. The tan 1 x 2 brick and door-rail plate build up the end of that wall (the rail is the groove seen on the finished model).
I identified the second icon as lego-32028 because it is the only tan 1 x 2 plate with a rail in the parts list. The exact studs covered are my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 35 adds two tan 1 x 2 plates stacked one on the other on top of the side-wall end (the callout), plus the pieces for a laptop and cushion on the sofa. These are a white 1 x 2 plate, the white 1 x 2 tile printed with a computer keyboard, and two black minifig neckwear brackets.
The two black pieces are read as Minifig Neckwear Bracket [One Stud] (lego-42446), the only black part with that shape in the parts list.
Which sofa pieces hold which of the new pieces is not clear from the small drawing. I recorded all four as resting on the sofa top plate (b144).

Step 36 adds a black 1 x 2 plate with angled handles, with a black 1 x 2 tile pressed onto it (the callout). Together they form the laptop on the sofa. It also adds a tan 1 x 2 tile on top of the stacked tan plates at the end of the side wall.
The black icon with side ears is read as Plate Special 1 x 2 with Angled Handles on Side (lego-92692), the only black 1 x 2 plate with handles of that shape in the parts list.
The black piece is placed on the white sofa plate from step 35 (b148). This is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 37 builds a small prop on the sofa. A white round 1 x 1 brick holds a dark bluish gray pistol (callout 1). A trans-yellow round 1 x 1 plate gets a light bluish gray tile with clip on top (the small inset in callout 2), and that clip is attached to the pistol (callout 2).
The yellow piece is Plate Round 1 x 1 in Trans-Yellow (lego-6141). The white cup-shaped icon is the white Brick Round 1 x 1 (lego-3062b), because that is the white round part in the parts list.
Where exactly the clip assembly sits is my best reading. I recorded the clip on the pistol as the join and the yellow plate as resting on the sofa plate b144.

Step 38 adds two medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry bricks and one medium nougat 1 x 1 brick, plus two tan 1 x 1 bricks and one tan 1 x 1 brick with a stud on one side (lego-87087). They build up the low wall and corner pillar beside the window.

The page shows no callout, only the finished model, and the stack is small and crowded. Which brick sits on which is my best reading. In particular, tiles cannot carry bricks, so I placed the tan bricks on the studs that remain on the 1 x 3 brick (b128) and the door-rail plate (b143).

Step 39 adds a medium nougat 1 x 4 masonry brick on top of the two masonry 1 x 2 bricks from step 38, and two tan 1 x 2 bricks stacked on the tan end column of the low wall. The page shows no callout, only the finished model.
Exactly which bricks the tan 1 x 2s sit on is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 40 repeats the same mix of parts as step 38. It adds two tan 1 x 1 bricks, one tan 1 x 1 brick with a side stud (lego-87087), two medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry bricks and one medium nougat 1 x 1 brick, raising the low wall and tan end column by another course.
The page shows no callout, only the finished model. Which brick each new piece sits on is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 41 adds another course along the back wall: one tan 1 x 8, two tan 1 x 3, three tan 1 x 2, one tan 2 x 2 corner brick and four tan 1 x 1 bricks with a side stud (lego-87087). The side-stud bricks are the round marks visible on the wall face.
The icons for the 2x and 3x bricks both show three studs, so I assumed the 2x are 1 x 3 (lego-3622) and the 3x are 1 x 2 (lego-3004). This matches the leftover counts in the parts list.
The page shows no callout, only the finished model. Which brick sits on which is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 42 adds a medium nougat 1 x 4 masonry brick, a medium nougat 1 x 2 masonry brick, a medium nougat 1 x 1 brick, a tan 1 x 1 brick and a tan 2 x 2 corner brick. These raise the right-hand masonry wall and the tan corner pillar.

The callout, marked 2x, shows a small stack of three: a tan 1 x 1 plate on top, a tan 1 x 1 plate with a horizontal clip in the middle, and a tan 1 x 1 plate at the bottom. It is built twice, using the four 1 x 1 tan plates and two clip plates. The clip faces sideways and is not used here, only as a decoration hook.
The stacks sit on the top of the masonry wall. Which brick carries each piece is my best reading of the small drawing.

Step 43 adds four reddish brown 1 x 1 plates, stacked in two pairs (callout 1), and a reddish brown 1 x 4 plate laid across the two stacks like a bridge (callout 2). Together they form a raised cap on the top of the bookshelf.
The callout arrow points at the top of the bookshelf. I placed the two stacks on the top shelf plate (b121), which is my best reading of the small drawing.
Step 44 builds a tall post. It is a 1 x 1 x 5 brick (lego-2453b) with a medium nougat 1 x 1 brick under it and another on top (callout 1). Callout 2 shows a sticker being applied to the post.
The post stands on the tan floor block near the sofa. I placed its bottom brick on b24 as a best guess.
The sticker sheet is a single part (b109). I recorded this second sticker as another join from the same sheet part to the post.

Step 45 adds four tan 1 x 8 bricks and a tan 1 x 3 brick. Three 1 x 8 bricks and the 1 x 3 extend the back wall by another course. One 1 x 8 becomes a header beam resting on the top of the tall post (b203) and the tan corner pillar (b189), forming a doorway-like arch.
It also adds two medium nougat 1 x 4 masonry bricks and a 1 x 2 masonry brick on the right masonry wall. The callout shows a medium nougat 1 x 1 brick being pushed onto the masonry corner.
The drawing is small and the wall is crowded, so which brick carries each new piece is my best reading.
Step 46 caps the walls with smooth tan tiles: four 1 x 8 tiles, two 1 x 4 tiles and three 1 x 2 tiles. They cover the tops of the studs on the back wall, the header beam and the right-hand walls.
It also adds the curtain rod, a light bluish gray rigid hose (lego-75c08). The callout shows it dropped across the window, resting over the masonry wall pieces.
The 3x, 4x and 2x tan tile icons are matched to the 1 x 2, 1 x 8 and 1 x 4 tile counts in the parts list. Which wall piece each tile covers is my best reading of the small drawing.
The top of the page is a preview of what bag 2 builds: four minifigures (Leonard, Sheldon, Raj, Penny) and the finished apartment with the furniture added. It places no bricks.
The lower part shows a minifigure (Leonard) being assembled from hair, head, torso and legs. As on page 15, none of those minifigure parts are in the parts list, so I recorded nothing for them.
Remaining parts from the parts list will be recorded on the next building pages.

Step 47 puts decorations on the bookshelf and the back wall. On top of the bookshelf, a black round 1 x 1 plate takes a trans-red cone (red flask), shown in the callout, and a blue 1 x 1 piece (blue flask) stands next to it.
The blue piece is read as the Blue Tap 1 x 1 (lego-4599b), since there is no blue cone in the parts list. I am not certain about this.

The dark gray printed tile with the joystick and control panel print, and the white 2 x 4 tile with the physics equations print, are pressed sideways onto the side studs of the side-stud bricks in the back wall. That is why they have rests_on as [] and are listed in other_joins.
Which individual side-stud bricks carry the tiles is my best reading of the picture.

Step 48 is a small sub-assembly built twice (2x). Each copy starts from a dark blue 1 x 6 tile held upside down. Step 1: a black plate with a clip is pressed onto it. Step 2: a black grille tile and a black round 1 x 1 plate are pressed on beside it. Step 3: the assembly is flipped over and a dark blue 1 x 1 tile goes on the stud of the round plate.

I matched the icons to the parts list as follows. The long dark blue strip is the Tile 1 x 6 with Groove (lego-6636). The black clip piece is the Plate Special 1 x 2 with Clip Horizontal on End (lego-63868). The grille piece is the Tile Special 1 x 2 Grille (lego-2412b). The black round piece is the Plate Round 1 x 1 (lego-6141). The small blue tile is the Tile 1 x 1 in Dark Blue (lego-3070b).
The assembly is built upside down, so the rests_on links are my best reading: each black piece sits against the blue tile, and the small blue tile sits on the round black plate.

Page 65 adds no new pieces. The two dark blue and black sub-assemblies built on page 64 (b228 to b232, and b233 to b237) are attached to the curtain rod from step 46 (b222). The arrows show one assembly hanging down by the window as a curtain and the other lying along the top of the bookshelf, with the clip end snapped onto the rod.
The side text (Howard quote) adds no pieces.
The second assembly (the blue strip on the bookshelf top) probably also rests on the shelf-top pieces. The drawing is too small for me to tell which, so I only recorded the clip joins.

Step 49 starts a separate small model: a double-helix (DNA) column, shown in the preview at the top. Step 1 puts a red round 2 x 2 plate on a reddish brown round 2 x 2 brick. Step 2 pushes the long white bar down through the middle. Step 3 adds the first blue tap on a stud of the red plate.

The parts box lists a blue round 2 x 2 plate, four red taps, four blue taps, a red round plate, a white bar and a brown round brick. Only the pieces actually placed in steps 1 to 3 are recorded here. The rest of the red and blue taps and the blue plate will be added on the following pages.
This column is not attached to the apartment, so the first brick (b238) rests on nothing. The white bar is a freestanding rod through the axle holes, so it also rests on nothing.

Pages 66 and 67 are the same build: steps 4 to 6 finish the DNA column started in step 49. Step 4 and step 5 stack the remaining taps up the white bar in two columns, one blue and one red. Step 6 puts the blue round 2 x 2 plate on top, which gives the column its twisted red and blue look.

I read the taps as simple stacks. Each tap sits on the stud of the one below, and the red column starts on the red plate (b239). The blue column continues from the blue tap placed in step 3 (b241), and the blue plate rests on the top tap of each column.
The picture shows alternating taps. The exact interleaving of the two columns is hard to tell from the small drawing. The totals match the parts list: four blue taps and four red taps in all.
Page 68 adds no new pieces. The arrow shows the finished DNA column from pages 66 and 67 being stood on the floor next to the bookshelf, on the reddish brown 1 x 4 plate (b20) from step 6.
The reddish brown round brick at the base of the column (b238) is not fastened to the plate, so I recorded this as a loose join in other_joins rather than a rests_on link.

Step 50 adds a blue 1 x 8 tile, a blue 1 x 1 tile, two dark bluish gray 1 x 1 tiles and two dark red 1 x 1 tiles. They lie on the floor on the long reddish brown 1 x 10 plate from step 10 (b33) and start the blue coffee-table or rug detail. The page shows no callout, only the finished model.

I read the two small dark red-brown icons as Tile 1 x 1 with Groove in Dark Red (lego-3070b), matching the dark red tiles in the parts list. Where exactly each tile sits along the plate is my best reading of the small drawing, so I listed b33 for all of them.

Step 51 completes the blue rug border on the floor. It adds one 1 x 1 tile, three 1 x 2 tiles, two 2 x 4 tiles and one 1 x 8 tile, all blue. They join the blue 1 x 8 tile and 1 x 1 tile from step 50 to form a rectangular blue frame around an open floor area.
